note: DRD Agent is the remote-agent side of Drupal Remote Dashboard (DRD). A central DRD portal calls its routes (/drd-agent main endpoint, /drd-agent-crypt, /drd-agent-authorize-secret, /drd-agent-authorize) over encrypted HTTP to run Action classes (Cron, FlushCache, MaintenanceMode, Info, Projects, Update, ...). Everything is stored in State (no config schema): drd_agent.debug_mode (settings form toggle), drd_agent.authorised (authorized dashboards), drd_agent.ott. Settings form drd_agent.settings.form at /admin/config/system/drd (perm 'administer site configuration'; module has no permissions of its own). Drush: drd:agent:setup <token> (alias drd-agent-setup). Defines plugin type drd_pi_auth (manager plugin.manager.drd_pi_auth, annotation @DrdPiAuth) with plugins acquia/pantheon/platformsh. Medium/hard cases are grounded in the module's State keys (drd_agent.debug_mode, drd_agent.authorised); baselines are restored by deleting the keys.

evals.prompt: What is the drd_agent module for, and what is the main HTTP endpoint a Drupal Remote Dashboard (DRD) instance calls on a site running it?
evals.expected_output: drd_agent is the agent installed on a remote Drupal site so a central DRD (Drupal Remote Dashboard) can connect and run maintenance/monitoring actions over encrypted HTTP. The main action endpoint is the /drd-agent route (Agent::get); it also exposes /drd-agent-crypt, /drd-agent-authorize-secret and /drd-agent-authorize.

evals.prompt: Which Drush command does drd_agent provide to configure a site to communicate with a DRD instance, and what argument does it take?
evals.expected_output: drush drd:agent:setup <token> (alias drd-agent-setup). The token is a base64- and JSON-encoded array of the variables DRD needs; on success it logs a portal URL to open to finish authorizing the agent.

evals.prompt: drd_agent defines a plugin type for authenticating against hosting-provider infrastructure. What is the plugin type / manager, and which provider plugins ship with it?
evals.expected_output: The drd_pi_auth plugin type (manager plugin.manager.drd_pi_auth, annotation @DrdPiAuth, dir Plugin/DrdPiAuth). It ships the acquia, pantheon, and platformsh plugins so DRD can reach sites on those platforms.

evals.prompt: Is DRD Agent's Debug mode currently enabled on this site? Inspect the live state and report the value.
evals.expected_output: Debug mode is enabled: State key drd_agent.debug_mode is TRUE (drush state:get drd_agent.debug_mode).

evals.prompt: A DRD dashboard has been authorized to control this site through the drd_agent module. Inspect the live agent state and give the key/id of the authorized dashboard entry.
evals.expected_output: The authorized dashboard is keyed drdmed_dash in the State value drd_agent.authorised (drush state:get drd_agent.authorised).

evals.prompt: Turn on DRD Agent's Debug mode on this site so its interactions with the DRD dashboard are logged for troubleshooting. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: State key drd_agent.debug_mode is TRUE — set via the DRD Agent settings form at /admin/config/system/drd (Debug mode checkbox) or `drush state:set drd_agent.debug_mode 1`.

evals.prompt: This site's drd_agent should trust a DRD dashboard identified by the key 'drdhard_dash'. Add an entry with that key to the agent's authorized-dashboards state (drd_agent.authorised). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The State array drd_agent.authorised contains a key 'drdhard_dash'. Read the current array (\Drupal::state()->get('drd_agent.authorised', [])), add the drdhard_dash entry, and save it back with \Drupal::state()->set('drd_agent.authorised', $array).
